result.title: AquaProbe: Efficient Adaptation of Frozen Vision Models for Underwater Images
result.summary: Reliable visual perception is essential for safe autonomous underwater exploration. Yet vision models pretrained on terrestrial images become less reliable underwater, where turbidity, backscatter, and wavelength-dependent attenuation alter scene appearance. Existing adaptation methods either spread adapters equally across the encoder depth or select layers using the divergence between two fixed domains. In this paper, we introduce AquaProbe for measuring how the location of the domain gap changes with water type and imaging range. AquaProbe separates newly introduced divergence from that accumulated through a frozen vision encoder using paired clean and physically rendered images and allocates a fixed LoRA budget according to the measured profile. The segmentation mean Intersection-over-Union (mIoU) for the proportional LoRA rank allocation, based on the measured profile, is 70.1; this is a better result than uniform LoRA rank allocation by 1.9 mIoU points while having the same parameter budget of 0.59 million adapter parameters. The three-way router, conditioned on estimated condition clusters, achieves 70.6 mIoU on the standard SUIM split and 63.4 AUDRC under held-out degradation.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 AquaProbe，用配对的干净图像与物理渲染水下图像，逐层测量冻结视觉编码器中新引入的域差异随水体类型与成像距离的变化，并按该 profile 分配固定的 LoRA 秩预算，另加一个基于条件聚类的三路路由器。
AI.relevance_reason: 逐层表征分歧的测量与按层分配适配预算，可能可供核查 LVR 中视觉细节在内部状态的层深分布、证据筛选与计算资源分配；但论文不涉及 latent 推理状态生成，联系偏间接，需进一步评估迁移价值。
